# aeneid-078 drafter notes (X.510–605)

51 units. Title `Aeneae furor. Inferiae`; part "The Rage of Aeneas (X.510–605)"; titleEn "The Rage of Aeneas —
Aeneid X.510–605". ¶ units: 510 only (Greenough's single paragraph start in this part). make_units.py prints no
warnings. `sc` not written.

## Misprints (rule 5b; t kept as printed, l/i corrected)
- **10.583 `terris. ”Vesano`** for `terris.” Vesano`. Handled as 077's 451/495: unit 580–583 (`Cui Liger: “Non
  Diomedis… his dabitur terris.`) closes Liger's speech in l/i with ”; the stray ” begins the t of unit 583–584
  (`”Vesano talia late / dicta volant Ligeri.`), whose l/i carry no mark. Note of 580 opens with the rule-5b sentence.
- **10.594 `deseris. ”Haec`** for `deseris.” Haec`. Same handling: unit 592–594 (`“Lucage… iuga deseris.`) closes
  Aeneas's speech in l/i; the stray ” begins the t of unit 594–595 (`”Haec ita fatus / arripuit biiugos;`). Note of
  592 opens with the rule-5b sentence ("As at 583").
- PAIRS = {580: 583, 592: 594}; mark balance checked over each pair.
- No other misprint found (checked every line for lowercase after a full stop, stray or unbalanced marks, odd letters).
  Kept as printed, not misprints: `Troïus` (Greenough's diaeresis; noted), `Euander`, `conlucens`, `adfore`,
  `exultans`, `sepulchro`, `volnera`, `inruit`, `adfatur`, `Volcani`, `biiugis`/`quadriiugis` (all Greenough's
  spellings, noted once each).

## Half-line
- 10.580 `Cui Liger:` noted in unit 580–583 in 077's wording for 490 ("one of the many unfinished lines (more than
  fifty) left in the poem at Virgil's death, as 490 in the last part"). Scanner UNRESOLVED there is for the scan step.

## Variants (Latin Library) and how handled
- 10.539 `insignibus armis` / `albis`: sense changes (armour vs. the priest's white insignia) — noted in n.
- 10.585 `hostem` / `hostis`: singular vs. accusative plural (at Lucagus vs. at both brothers) — noted in one clause.
  Reviewer may judge this too slight to keep.
- 10.522 `ac` / `at`: no real change of sense — not noted.
- 10.581 `Achillis` / `Achilli`: both genitives of Achilles — morphology, not noted.
- 10.588 `aptet` / `aptat`: subjunctive (purpose-coloured `dum`) vs. indicative; no real change — not noted; n explains
  the subjunctive.
- 10.512 word order (`versis tempus` / `tempus versis`), 10.568 `enses`/`ensis`, and the orthographic ones
  (natoque/gnatoque, natis/gnatis, exultans, sepulchro, volnera, Troïus): not noted as variants.

## Readings I am less than sure of
- 10.517 `Sulmone creatos`: n gives both "sons of a man Sulmo" and "born at a town Sulmo"; `quos educat Ufens` taken
  as the river (present tense, home country), not the leader Ufens of VII.745.
- 10.541 `ingenti umbra tegit`: n gives both (death's darkness / Aeneas's shadow standing over him).
- 10.547–548 `vimque adfore verbo crediderat`: n suggests a spell or vow may be meant ("perhaps"); not sure what
  Conington prefers.
- 10.552–553 `reducta… hasta… impedit`: taken as the spear pinning corselet and shield together.
- 10.586–587 `telo admonuit biiugos`: taken as prodding the horses with his sword (no whip).
- 10.594 `ipse rotis saliens`: taken as Aeneas's sneer (Lucagus was struck and fell; Aeneas says he jumped).
- 10.599 `Pluribus oranti`: left open whether Liger is still speaking or about to.

## Attributions written from memory, not checked against a text
- Achilles takes twelve Trojan youths alive for Patroclus's pyre, Iliad 21.26–32; killed at the pyre, 23.175–176.
- The sacrifice carried out in Book XI (no line given); Mezentius's arms as a trophy at the start of Book XI.
- Adrastus begs Menelaus with ransom, Iliad 6.45–50; Lycaon begs Achilles, Iliad 21.64–96; Achilles' answer (spared
  before Patroclus died, now none), 21.99–105; Lycaon thrown in the river, no mother, fish lick the wound, 21.122–127.
- Palinurus `per spes surgentis Iuli`, VI.364.
- A Rutulian Sulmo killed in Book IX; Ufens a river of Latium.
- Caeculus son of Vulcan, founder of Praeneste; Umbro the Marsian snake-charming priest (Book VII catalogue).
- Faunus father of Latinus (Book VII).
- Amyclae's silence story (forbade talk of enemies after false alarms) — this is Servius's story, written without
  naming him, since Servius is not on the list of aids; reviewer may want to cut or confirm.
- A Camers alive again in Book XII (XII.224, Juturna takes his form) — the inconsistency is stated in n.
- Briareus/Aegaeon, Iliad 1.401–404; the version where he fights Jupiter.
- Diomedes wounds Aeneas and takes his horses, Iliad 5.297–327; Poseidon saves him from Achilles, 20.288–340.
- Suppliants under the protection of Zeus (general Homeric statement).
- "More than fifty" half-lines (as in 075/077).

## Decisions
- Advisory: none. `claude/content-advisory.md` was not opened (not in this checkout per 077's notes and QUESTIONS 36,
  40); decided on conventions.md's summary (sexual violence always; graphic detail rarely; ordinary battle killing
  earns nothing). The killing of suppliants (Mago, Tarquitus, Liger) is battle killing told without lingering. The
  taking of eight living youths for human sacrifice (517–520) is the one thing beyond ordinary killing: four lines,
  stated, not described (the act itself is in Book XI). I judged it below the "graphic detail" bar and gave it no
  advisory; the n of 517 states plainly what Aeneas does and names the Iliad model, no softening. QUESTIONS item 61
  stays open for the owner; if he wants human sacrifice to carry an advisory, it applies here and to the Book XI part.
- No set piece judged to fall in X.510–605. `Morere et fratrem ne desere frater` (600) is the most quotable line;
  drafted from the Latin, not proposed as a house rendering.
- Splits: 540–542 at `tegit;` (the killing / the trophy); 545–549 at `orbem;`; 575–577 at `Liger;`; 586–590 at
  `inguen:` (590 its own unit, to stay inside five lines). `Dixerat.` (530) its own unit, as in earlier parts.
  Liger's whole speech (580–583) kept in one unit with `Cui Liger:` so the misprint pair is unit-to-unit.
- `pius Aeneas` (591) rendered "dutiful Aeneas" (earlier parts vary: loyal / devoted / dutiful / pious).
